points: "Search the streets of Yerushalayim": if you find even one person who does justice, Hashem will forgive the city. Even more than Avraham asking for ten in Sedom.
The Abarbanel: there were good people, but none brave enough to rebuke others. "Live and let live" isn't enough; we are responsible for each other, with tact.
Rabbi Binyamin Lau: this is from Yoshiyahu's revival, when people changed only on the outside. They said "Baruch Hashem" and swore in His name but didn't mean it.
Next to idolatry and adultery, the sin listed is ignoring the downtrodden. Caring for the invisible people is the sign of a just society.
"Hanevi'im nibu vasheker... v'ami ahavu chen": a false prophet is one the people like. If the people who inspire us only make us comfortable, we're not growing.
